text:
incident-bot: ALERT: SLO burn rate exceeded threshold for /v1/generate in hosted-east-1. 12m burn = 3.2x, 1m spike also high. Paging sre-oncall. Dashboard: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/abcd/slo-burn

morgan (oncall): acked. I'm on it. any idea if this is customer-facing errors or internal retries?

anya (sre): looking at the traces — 50% increase in 5xx at the runtime layer, mostly 503/timeout from model-serving. latency p50 -> 220ms, p95 -> 1.2s. Not obviously downstream DB.

sam (platform): we just pushed the canary selector change at 07:10 UTC that routes ~15% of traffic to model-variant-quantv2. Could be related.

lee (eng): thanks, re-checking canary logs. I see elevated kv-cache-miss rates and a few kernel OOM warnings in the canary containers around 07:11-07:14. Paste logs:

```
07:11:22 kernel: OutOfMemoryError: GPU0: allocated 11.3GB but only 10.9GB free
07:11:23 runtime: kvcache miss ratio 0.72 (baseline ~0.05)
07:12:01 model-loader: falling back to slower quantized path
```

amanda (product): are there upstream customer complaints? I haven't seen any support tickets yet but our error budget alert is noisy. any ETA to reduce pages? customers might notice if p95 stays high.

morgan (oncall): plan: (1) mute low-priority alerts that are flooding (non-paging), (2) momentarily widen SLO burn paging criteria to avoid paging for brief canary regressions while we triage, (3) rollback or scale canary if confirmed. I'll create a temp dashboard and run a focused query.

ops-bot: @morgan acknowledged on-call handoff. Current oncall shift: morgan until 08:00 UTC.

morgan (oncall): muting noisy monitors now: datadog -> mute monitor ids 1201,1202. Command: 

```
datadog monitors mute 1201 1202 --message "muting noisy low-sev monitors during SLO burn triage (oncall)"
```

morgan (oncall): adjusting burn-rate alert to avoid immediate paging: increasing 1m threshold from 2.5x -> 4.0x and keeping 12m at 2.0x so we still capture sustained regressions. Applied via console.

anya (sre): thanks. I'll spin up extra canary capacity and pin canary to older quantization profile to test if quantv2 is the cause. If restore reduces kv-cache misses, we can either rollback or pause rollout.

lee (eng): confirmed: when routing back to quantv1 the OOMs stop in test cluster. suspect memory footprint regression in quantv2. I'm preparing a rollback patch.

morgan (oncall): temporary mitigation: scaled canary down from 15% -> 2% at 07:22 UTC. Noted in audit.

amanda (product): doing a quick customer impact assessment: no major accounts have reported errors yet. Slack alerts to support are low. we should still log an incident note for transparency.

sam (platform): creating a short-lived dashboard with these panels: p95 latency, kv-cache-miss ratio, model-ooms, requests by model-variant. link: https://grafana.internal/d/efgh/quick-slo-triage

morgan (oncall): good. please add a panel showing burn across multi-windows (1m/12m/60m). We should consider new monitor that pages only on multi-window correlation (e.g., >2x on 12m and >1.5x on 60m) to reduce single-minute flakiness.

anya (sre): created a jira: INF-2345 for postmortem and alerting changes. Proposed follow-ups: (a) add a multi-window burn monitor, (b) update paging policy doc to include canary-exemption window, (c) add automation to auto-scale canary back on kv-cache regressions.

lee (eng): rollback patch applied at 07:29 UTC, canary reverted to quantv1. metrics trending back to baseline now — p95 down to 320ms and kv-cache-miss ratio falling.

incident-bot: UPDATE: SLO burn reduced. 12m burn -> 1.05x at 07:34 UTC. Auto-resolve policy will clear paging if sustained.

morgan (oncall): handing off to night oncall (jules) at 07:45 UTC with follow-ups: keep muted monitors muted until postmortem, monitor the quick dashboard, if burn >1.8x on 12m re-escalate. Posting runbook link: https://wiki.internal/redwood/runbooks/slo-burn

amanda (product): thanks everyone — please include customer impact check and communications draft in INF-2345.

anya (sre): adding recommended alert config snippet for multi-window monitor to the ticket:

```
# pseudocode for new burn monitor
if burn_12m > 2.0 and burn_60m > 1.5 then page(sre-oncall)
else if burn_12m > 2.0 then notify(sre-team)
```

morgan (oncall): noted. filing a short post-incident action item list in INF-2345. closing thread once handoff complete.

ops-bot: oncall handoff recorded: from morgan to jules at 07:45 UTC.

morgan (oncall): thanks team. leaving monitor notes and links in the ticket.

lee (eng): will follow up on quantv2 memory regression; plan to add unit test for kv-cache pressure scenarios.

amanda (product): marking for customer comms review after postmortem.

incident-bot: THREAD CLOSED (automated) — SLO burn returned to normal and page cleared.
